records.name: Manual Time Entry
records.description: A logged-in user starts in the Time Tracking section with no matching entries visible for the last 30 days. They open the New time entry form, enter 10 hours and 33 minutes for 2 Aug 2026, select Project #254, choose the task "3D visualization," and create the entry. The system closes the modal, displays the new time record in the time-tracking list, updates the totals to 10h 33m, and shows a confirmation toast.
records.problem:
From the user's perspective, the task is to manually record time spent working on a specific project task. The user needs to provide a duration and date, then associate the time with the relevant project and task before saving. Optional phase and note fields are available but are not completed in the shown path.

From the interface perspective, the system provides an empty-state Time Tracking view, opens a side-panel form for creating a time entry, progressively reveals additional fields after a project is selected, and allows the user to submit the completed record. After submission, the system adds the entry to the list, recalculates the displayed totals, and confirms that the entry was added.

The user-perceived outcome is that their 10-hour, 33-minute work session is successfully logged against the selected project task. The system-level outcome is a new time record dated 2 Aug 2026, associated with Project #254 and the task "3D visualization," included in the displayed studio and personal totals.

content.description:
The screen is a minimalist, light-themed time tracking dashboard with a two-column application layout. The overall visual style is calm, spacious, and professional, using a neutral palette dominated by off-white and soft grays with dark charcoal accents. The main background is a very light warm gray/ivory, approximately #FAFAFA, while text uses deep charcoal #24241D and secondary text uses muted gray-brown tones such as #706F6B and #9C9C97. Accent details appear in a warm beige-brown #867569, with subtle borders in very light gray and soft shadowing throughout.

The left sidebar is fixed, narrow, and vertically stacked on a pale gray background that is slightly darker than the main canvas. It contains a company area at the top, then a search row and quick actions, followed by a navigation menu with small monochrome icons and labels. Active navigation states are shown with a soft highlighted pill/row and darker text, while inactive items remain muted. Some items have badges, such as a small numeric badge near “Pulse” and a green “New” badge near “Presentations.” The sidebar uses compact typography, likely a clean sans-serif at around 12–14 px for menu items and 14–16 px for section labels. Icons are small, simple, and line-based, rendered in dark gray.

Near the bottom of the sidebar there is a help pill featuring tiny avatar thumbnails, the text “Need help?”, and a small status dot. Below that are secondary links like “What’s new” and “Guides.” At the very bottom sits a dark upgrade card with a near-black background (#24241D or close), white text, a small note such as “5 days left,” and a prominent light button labeled “Upgrade.” This card uses strong contrast to draw attention and has rounded corners.

The main content area is mostly empty, emphasizing a blank-state dashboard. At the top left of the content area, a subtle breadcrumb or section label reads “Time Tracking” beside a small square icon. Center-left in the header zone is the page title “Time Tracking” set in a serif or serif-like display typeface, larger than all other text and visually elegant, likely around 28–36 px with medium/light weight. Beneath it is a date-range filter chip labeled “Last 30 days,” with a tiny calendar icon inside a rounded rectangle. On the upper right of the content header are compact actions: a text link “Export,” a dark filled primary button “New entry,” and below them a grouping control labeled “Group by Date” with a dropdown chevron and a small square filter/settings icon button.

The page’s center shows an empty state for the results area. A small loading/search-like icon sits above the message “No results,” followed by lighter helper text reading “No time entry matched your filter.” Beneath that is a small outlined button labeled “Clear filter.” The empty state is centered horizontally and vertically within the otherwise blank workspace, reinforcing the absence of data. The typography here is smaller, likely 12–14 px for the status text and 14–16 px for the action button. The button has a light border, white background, and dark text, with subtle hover/active states implied by gentle shadow or border darkening.

In the top-right corner of the interface there is a compact timer/clock widget inside a rounded capsule. It displays the current time “17:28:07” and an adjacent orange circular indicator/icon, suggesting active time tracking or recording. The capsule has a white background, subtle shadow, and minimal border, matching the soft aesthetic of the rest of the interface.

The layout uses strong whitespace, with the sidebar taking roughly one quarter of the width and the main workspace occupying the rest. All containers use large corner radii, soft shadows, and restrained borders. The composition feels like a productivity SaaS admin panel, designed to be unobtrusive, readable, and efficient.

The screen uses a two-column layout. The left column is a fixed vertical sidebar, approximately 20–25% of the width, divided into several stacked groups: brand/header, utility actions, primary navigation, contextual help, secondary links, and a promotional upgrade card. Each group is separated by spacing rather than hard dividers, creating a soft modular structure.

The right main column occupies the remaining width and is a large content canvas with a simple header area and a centered empty-state region. At the top of the main column, the page header is aligned left while action buttons are aligned right, forming a single horizontal header row. Beneath the title, the date filter sits left of center, and the export/new-entry actions sit in the upper-right zone. A grouping control is placed below or near the actions, also aligned to the right. content.description:

The body contains a vertically stacked form with crisp section spacing and thin light-gray field borders. The first row has two equal-width numeric inputs placed side by side: “Hours” on the left and “Minutes” on the right. Both fields have compact text-entry styling, white fill, faint gray borders, and dark text values (“10” and “33”). The next field is a full-width date input labeled “Date,” with a small calendar icon on the left and the selected date “2 Aug 2026” inside the field. Below that is a full-width “Project” dropdown showing “Project #254” with a right-side chevron/selector indicator. Then come two optional dropdown fields labeled “Phase (Optional)” and “Task (Optional),” each with a placeholder or selected value; “Phase” shows “Select phase” in muted gray placeholder text, while “Task” shows “3D visualization” in dark text. The last control is a larger multiline “Note (Optional)” text area with the placeholder “Add an optional note...”, sized to allow several lines of text and visually separated by a taller border box.

Field labels are small, dark gray, and positioned above each input with consistent spacing, likely 12–14 px. Optional labels are indicated in lighter gray and parentheses, reducing visual weight. Inputs have generous internal padding, slightly rounded corners, and subtle hover/active states implied by the clean border treatment; no heavy accents or bright colors are used, keeping the screen focused and professional.

At the bottom-right of the modal is a compact action row with two buttons. “Cancel” is a secondary button with a light/outlined treatment and dark text, while “Create” is the primary button with a dark filled background (#252422 or near-black) and white text, making it the dominant action. The buttons are small to medium in height, aligned horizontally with a small gap, and anchored to the dialog footer.

The dimmed background reveals a left sidebar navigation and a page title “Time Tracking” in the main content area, but these are intentionally subdued and blurred by the modal overlay. The overall visual style is modern, understated, and utility-focused, with strong hierarchy, ample whitespace, thin dividers, and a restrained monochrome palette.

At the broader level, this interface enables users to maintain accurate time records inside a project management or time tracking system. The dimmed background and centered dialog help maintain focus and prevent accidental navigation while the entry is being completed.

content.description:
The screen is a clean, minimal productivity dashboard for time tracking, built with a soft neutral palette and subtle card-based hierarchy. The overall visual style is calm, editorial, and modern, with generous white space, very light gray surfaces, thin dividers, rounded corners, and restrained accent colors. The interface is dominated by off-white and light gray backgrounds, with dark charcoal text used for primary emphasis and muted taupe/stone tones for secondary labels and icons.

Color palette: the main canvas background is a very pale warm gray/white, close to #FAFAFA. The left sidebar uses a slightly darker warm gray background with faint borders and separators. Primary text appears in deep charcoal, approximately #24241D. Secondary and inactive text use muted gray tones around #6E6E6A and #9C9C97. Accent and interactive highlights use a warm beige/taupe tone around #877569. Buttons include a dark filled button for the primary action, likely #24241D with white text, and lighter outlined or text-style actions for secondary controls. The toast notification at bottom-right uses a white card with a green success dot and dark text; the success indicator is a small bright green accent.

Typography is highly legible and understated. The page title “Time Tracking” is set in a large serif or serif-like display font, likely around 28–34 px, with medium weight and generous letter spacing/line height, creating a premium editorial feel. Sidebar labels and utility text appear in a small sans-serif font, roughly 12–14 px, regular weight, with compact line height. Table and metric labels are similarly compact and refined, using gray tones to reduce visual noise. The hierarchy is clear: large serif title, medium metric values, then small descriptive labels.

Layout and structure: the screen uses a two-column layout. A fixed left sidebar occupies about 20–25% of the width, while the main content area takes the remaining space. The sidebar is vertically stacked with grouped navigation links, each with a small icon and label, separated by subtle spacing and section breaks. The active item, “Time Tracking,” is highlighted with a light rounded pill background and stronger text contrast. A top area in the sidebar contains the workspace name (“Company”) and a small switch/selector icon. Lower in the sidebar there is a help module with tiny overlapping avatars, a “Need help?” button, a small support status dot, and a promotional upgrade card at the bottom with dark background and a white “Upgrade” button.

In the main content area, the top row contains the page title aligned toward the upper left, with utility actions on the right: a text link for Export and a dark primary button labeled New entry. A compact live timer appears in the top-right corner of the window inside a rounded chip, showing elapsed time and a small orange status/control indicator. Below the title is a filter chip for “Last 30 days” with a calendar icon, and on the right a “Group by Date” dropdown with a small chevron and a separate small filter/settings icon button.

The central content is a single summary card with soft shadow, thin border, and rounded corners. Inside the card, the top section contains two large metric blocks laid out horizontally: “10h 33m Studio total” and “10h 33m Your total.” The values are bold and prominent, with labels beneath in smaller muted text. A horizontal divider separates these totals from the time-entry list below. The list is grouped by date, showing “Sunday, 2 Aug, 2026” on the left and the daily total “10h 33m” aligned to the right. Under that, one visible entry row shows a small initials avatar badge (“LB”), the task or project name “3D visualization,” and on the far right the project label “Project #254” plus the duration “10h 33m.” The row is cleanly aligned with ample spacing, using light gray borders and subtle row separation.

The bottom-right toast notification is a floating success message with rounded corners and a soft shadow. It contains a green status dot, the message “Time entry added,” and a close icon on the far right. The toast sits above the canvas and does not obstruct the main content.

The design is intentionally sparse, with no decorative imagery. Shadows are soft and minimal, borders are hairline-thin, and corners are moderately rounded across chips, cards, buttons, and notifications. The spacing system is consistent, with medium padding inside cards and larger outer margins around the main content area. Overall, the screen feels like a polished work-management product with a strong focus on clarity, time reporting, and quick entry actions.
content.layout:
Two-column desktop dashboard layout with a fixed left navigation sidebar and a large main workspace on the right. The sidebar spans the full height and is organized into stacked groups: top workspace header, utility links, primary navigation list, nested sub-navigation under Studio, support/help module, secondary links, and a bottom upgrade promo card. The active nav item is shown with a rounded highlight.

The main content column uses a centered, spacious composition with strong top padding and a narrow content width relative to the full canvas. The title sits near the upper left of the content area. Action controls are aligned on the same horizontal level near the upper right. Beneath that is a row of filtering controls, with the date-range chip on the left and grouping/filter controls on the right. The central card is placed below with ample whitespace around it, creating a floating, uncluttered dashboard feel. The card contains a two-part metric header and a grouped list/table section beneath. A toast notification floats in the bottom-right corner above the page content. The overall grid is simple: sidebar column plus main content region, with the main region internally arranged in a header row, a filter row, and one primary content card.
content.functions:
This interface lets users review and manage tracked work time. At the smallest level, users can inspect time summaries, change the reporting range with the date filter, switch grouping behavior with the Group by Date control, export data, and create a new time entry using the primary button. The timer chip in the header communicates that a time-tracking session or live clock is active, helping users monitor time in real time.

At a workflow level, the screen supports reviewing a period of tracked work, understanding totals at both studio and personal levels, and inspecting individual logged entries grouped by day. The list row shows the task/project name, associated project code, and duration, which helps users audit how time was spent. The navigation sidebar allows movement to related workspace modules like projects, presentations, financials, libraries, to-do lists, and the studio management area, making this screen part of a broader productivity suite.

At a broader level, the screen helps teams and individuals record billable or internal work time, organize entries by date, and gain a concise overview of time allocation. It is designed for quick logging, lightweight review, and easy export, making it useful for project tracking, productivity analysis, and reporting. The interface emphasizes speed and clarity, reducing friction when users need to add entries, verify totals, and manage time records efficiently.
